issues.t: Clunk from the steering intermediate shaft
issues.sym: A clunk or knock felt through the steering wheel, most noticeable when turning slowly, parking, or going over small bumps.
issues.why: The sliding steering shaft between the column and the steering gear wears and develops play. GM issued a long-running bulletin series that replaces the upper intermediate shaft.
issues.next: Have the shaft checked for looseness. It is usually a noise annoyance, but any looseness in the steering should be inspected.

issues.t: ABS light from a failing brake control module
issues.sym: ABS and brake warning lights stay on, stability messages appear, and ABS may kick in at low speed when it should not.
issues.why: The ABS control module or its connections develop faults, and dirty wheel speed sensor mounting surfaces can send false signals. GM published bulletins for these codes.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read. Normal braking usually still works, but anti-lock protection may be off, so get it fixed soon.

issues.t: Gauge needles sticking or reading wrong
issues.sym: The speedometer, fuel gauge, or other needles freeze, read wrong, or swing randomly, and the cluster may be slow to come on.
issues.why: The tiny motors that move the gauge needles wear out on this generation's instrument cluster.
issues.next: A cluster rebuild or replacement fixes it. Do not trust the speedometer or fuel gauge until it is repaired.

issues.t: Door handles breaking off
issues.sym: Inside or outside door handles snap or come loose, and the door may not open from one side.
issues.why: The handle parts on early models of this generation are brittle and break with normal use.
issues.next: Replace the broken handle. Make sure every door can still be opened from inside in case of an emergency.

issues.t: Ignition lock can bind (recall)
issues.sym: The key is hard to turn or sticks in the start position. If it springs back to accessory, the engine can shut off while driving.
issues.why: The ignition lock actuator can bind. If the engine shuts off, power steering and brake assist are lost and air bags may not deploy.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the lock housing replaced. If the key sticks, get it fixed before driving further.

issues.t: Cylinder deactivation lifter failure
issues.sym: A tapping or ticking from the engine, misfire codes, rough idle, check engine light, or loss of power.
issues.why: The special lifters that let the engine shut off cylinders to save fuel can stick or collapse, which can wear the camshaft.
issues.next: Get it diagnosed promptly. A collapsed lifter can damage the camshaft if you keep driving on it.

issues.t: Shudder from the 8-speed automatic
issues.sym: A vibration like driving over rumble strips at steady cruising speeds with light throttle, plus harsh or clunky shifts.
issues.why: The torque converter clutch shudders as it locks up. GM's fix is a complete fluid flush with a revised fluid; a top-off does not help.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the transmission against the shudder bulletin. Note that the 8-speed arrived partway through 2015; earlier 2015s have a 6-speed.

issues.t: Magnetic Ride shocks leaking
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, a harsh or bouncy ride, oily shock bodies, or a Service Suspension System message.
issues.why: The electronically controlled shocks develop internal faults and leak.
issues.next: Have the shocks inspected and ask about GM's bulletin for leaking shocks.

issues.t: A/C condenser leaking refrigerant
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, often coming back soon after a recharge, with oily residue at the front of the radiator area.
issues.why: The combined A/C condenser and transmission cooler can crack from repeated heating and cooling. GM extended coverage on affected vehicles.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether your VIN is covered by the special coverage before paying for the repair.

issues.t: Reduced brake assist from vacuum pump (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly feels hard and needs much more effort, and stopping distances get longer.
issues.why: The engine-driven vacuum pump that powers the brake booster can lose output over time. The recall reprograms the brake module to add hydraulic assist when vacuum drops.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A hard brake pedal should be checked right away; drive gently until it is.

issues.t: 6.2L rod and crankshaft defect (recall)
issues.sym: A knock that rises with engine speed, low oil pressure warnings, rough running, or sudden power loss or engine seizure.
issues.why: Manufacturing defects in the crankshaft and connecting rods. GM recalled affected engines for inspection, with repair or replacement if needed and a thicker oil for engines that pass.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the engine knocks or the oil pressure warning comes on, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Center screen going black
issues.sym: The large curved display goes black with a warning symbol, and camera views and infotainment stop working.
issues.why: Software glitches in the video processing module. GM issued a bulletin to reset and reprogram it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for the software update.

issues.t: Rear wheels can lock up (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden rear-wheel lockup or skid while driving, sometimes with transmission warnings or reduced power.
issues.why: A control valve in the 10-speed automatic can fail. GM recalled 2022 models (and 2021 diesels) for new transmission software.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free software update promptly.

issues.t: Transfer case missing part (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: Grinding or binding from under the vehicle, or a sudden lockup of the front or rear wheels.
issues.why: A small number of 4WD and AWD vehicles were built with a part missing from the transfer case, which can lock the wheels without warning.
issues.next: Check your VIN right away. If it is included, do not drive the vehicle until the dealer repairs it.

issues.t: Battery cable can rub on the steering shaft (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from under the hood, flickering electrics, or a no-start.
issues.why: On some all-wheel-drive trucks the positive battery cable was not clipped in place. It can rub through on the steering shaft and short out, which can start a fire.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Cadillac dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Steering and brake pedal suddenly get heavy (recall)
issues.sym: The steering wheel and brake pedal take much more effort than normal, usually without warning.
issues.why: A seal inside the hydraulic brake booster, which shares fluid with the power steering, can break because a bore was machined out of tolerance.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Cadillac or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Power steering hose can split (recall)
issues.sym: Red or amber fluid under the front, heavy steering, a hard brake pedal, or smoke from the engine bay.
issues.why: A power steering hose that was not made to specification can crack. The fluid loss takes away steering and brake assist, and fluid on hot parts can catch fire.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Cadillac dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Heated washer fluid module can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A hot plastic smell or smoke from the front of the engine bay, or washers that stop working.
issues.why: The module that warms the washer fluid can short internally and overheat. GM recalled it twice and in the end removed the heater.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Cadillac dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Fuel pump control module lets water in (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls, will not start, or cranks without firing, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: The seal on the fuel pump control module under the truck can come apart. Water then gets inside and the module stops running the fuel pump.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Cadillac or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Rear axle can lock up (recall)
issues.sym: A bang or grinding from the rear axle, then the rear wheels suddenly dragging or locking.
issues.why: A pin inside the rear differential was not hardened correctly. It can break or slide out of place and jam the axle.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Cadillac dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Shifter can move out of Park on its own (recall)
issues.sym: The truck can be shifted out of Park with the key off or out, or rolls after parking.
issues.why: A faulty park lock cable or steering column lock part may not hold the shifter in Park.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time you park, and have a Cadillac dealer do the free recall repair right away.

issues.t: Chassis control module can short out (recall)
issues.sym: Stalling, a no-start, or warning lights that come and go.
issues.why: Contamination inside the chassis electronic module, which runs the fuel pump, can cause an internal short.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Cadillac or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Power steering assist cuts out and snaps back (recall)
issues.sym: The steering goes heavy for a moment and then the assist returns suddenly, most often at low speed.
issues.why: A brief voltage drop can make the electric power steering shut off and then come back on abruptly.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Cadillac dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Front airbags may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing beforehand; sometimes an airbag warning light.
issues.why: A software fault in the airbag control module can leave it stuck in a self-test, so the front airbags and seat belt tighteners do not fire in a crash.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Cadillac dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Front upper control arm weld can fail (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front end, loose or wandering steering, or a front wheel that looks tilted.
issues.why: The weld holding the bushing to a front upper control arm may be too weak, so the arm can come apart from the bushing.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Cadillac dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Fuel pump built without a pressure regulator (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell, fuel dripping near the tank, or a check engine light.
issues.why: Some in-tank fuel pumps were assembled without the pressure regulator, so pressure can climb high enough to cause a leak.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Cadillac dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Fuel pump power module can quit (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not restart.
issues.why: The module that powers the fuel pump can fail, cutting fuel to the engine.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Cadillac or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Rear driveshaft can break (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration or a clunk from underneath, then the truck stops pulling even though the engine revs.
issues.why: Parts inside the rear driveshaft missed their heat treatment and can fail.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Cadillac dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: Diesel models may have the wrong fuel tank (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing in normal driving. The risk is a fuel leak after a rollover crash.
issues.why: Some diesel trucks may have been built with a fuel tank that was not meant for them.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Cadillac or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Rear control arm bolts can snap (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the rear, the truck steering itself from the back, or uneven rear tire wear.
issues.why: Bolts for the rear outer control arms were not hardened correctly and can break, letting a rear wheel go out of line.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Cadillac dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.

issues.t: No warning when brake fluid is low (recall)
issues.sym: No brake warning light even though the fluid level has dropped; the pedal may feel soft or travel further.
issues.why: Brake control software may fail to turn on the warning when fluid is lost.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the Cadillac or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free recall repair if it is still open.

issues.t: Front wheel hub bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking, a clunk or vibration from a front wheel, mainly on trucks with the largest factory wheels.
issues.why: The wrong bolts may have been used on the front hubs. They can stretch or back out.
issues.next: Do not put this off. Check the VIN with a Cadillac dealer or on the NHTSA recall site and get the free repair done right away.
